Formulation:
Predisposing: None identified.  
Precipitating: Sudden onset unilateral headache; no clear trigger noted.  
Perpetuating: Pain impairs daily functioning; no mental health factors identified.  
Protective: Lives with partner; willing to seek medical help.

Mental Health Care Plan Details
(No mental health problems identified; plan therefore focuses on monitoring for any emerging psychological distress related to ongoing pain.)

Principal Problem: Monitoring for potential mood/anxiety impact of persistent pain
- Patient Goal(s): Maintain normal daily functioning and well-being; seek help promptly if mood or anxiety symptoms emerge
- Clinical Goal(s): Screen for mood/anxiety symptoms at follow-up; provide education on pain-related psychological effects
- Actions (Patient): Track mood, sleep, and stress levels; report any sustained low mood, anxiety, or functional decline
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Reassess headache; administer brief mental health screen at next review; consider referral if psychological distress identified

Secondary Problem: New-onset headache (migraine vs tension-type)
- Patient Goal(s): Achieve pain relief; return to full work capacity
- Clinical Goal(s): Provide effective analgesia; monitor for red-flag symptoms; arrange further work-up if pain persists
- Actions (Patient): Use prescribed NSAID with food; add paracetamol as directed; maintain hydration/rest; seek review if worsening or new symptoms
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Supply prescription; safety-net instructions; schedule follow-up or urgent review if red-flag symptoms occur

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention:
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Headache red-flags, medication use, hydration, rest
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Increasing headache intensity, new neurological symptoms, fever, rash, vomiting, neck stiffness
- Coping Strategies: Rest, adequate hydration, prescribed analgesia; monitor stress levels

Consent, Coordination & Review:
- Patient Consent to Plan: Not recorded
- Copy of Mental Health Care Plan Given to Patient: Not recorded
- Other Mental Health Professionals Involved in Patient Care: None at present
- GP Acknowledgment (if completed by other MH Professional): Not applicable
- Review Date: Not recorded (GP advised patient to call back within 1–2 days if no improvement)

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)
- Migraine without aura – High likelihood: Unilateral throbbing headache, family history, age/sex profile
- Tension-type headache – Medium likelihood: Common, but pain character less typical
- Cervicogenic headache – Medium-Low likelihood: Unilateral occipital pain; sedentary occupation may contribute

Quality checks
● Missing but clinically expected elements: Comprehensive MSE, risk assessment, documented consent, review date  
● Internal conflicts: None between transcript and DDx  
● Transcript quality notes: Physical-health-focused consultation; no direct mental health assessment, so many sections marked “Not recorded.”
